questions.stem: The small, round, deeply basophilic inclusions within several red cells on this smear are which structures, and their persistence indicates what functional state?

explanation.summary: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear DNA remnants normally removed by a functioning spleen. Their presence signals the absent or non-functioning spleen (functional asplenia) seen in sickle cell disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear DNA remnants normally removed by a functioning spleen. Their presence signals the absent or non-functioning spleen (functional asplenia) seen in sickle cell disease.

questions.stem: On this cellulose acetate gel, hemoglobin variants migrate to different positions. HbS is separated from normal HbA primarily because of a difference in what property?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Electrical charge (HbS is less negatively charged)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iron content of the heme groups

explanation.summary: The glutamate-to-valine substitution removes a negative charge, so HbS migrates less far toward the anode than HbA in an electric field. Electrophoresis therefore separates hemoglobins mainly by charge.
explanation.whyCorrect: The glutamate-to-valine substitution removes a negative charge, so HbS migrates less far toward the anode than HbA in an electric field. Electrophoresis therefore separates hemoglobins mainly by charge.

questions.stem: This illustration of rigid sickled cells lodged within a small blood vessel depicts the mechanism underlying which major consequence of sickle cell disease?

explanation.summary: Sickled cells lose flexibility and become trapped in capillaries, blocking blood flow. The resulting ischemia and infarction of downstream tissue is termed vaso-occlusive disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sickled cells lose flexibility and become trapped in capillaries, blocking blood flow. The resulting ischemia and infarction of downstream tissue is termed vaso-occlusive disease.

questions.stem: In this schematic, HbS molecules aggregate into long strands when blood becomes deoxygenated, distorting the cell. What molecular process deforms the red blood cell into a sickle shape?

explanation.summary: In the taut, deoxygenated state the exposed hydrophobic valine residues cause HbS molecules to line up into rigid polymers. These insoluble strands physically contort the RBC into a sickle shape.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the taut, deoxygenated state the exposed hydrophobic valine residues cause HbS molecules to line up into rigid polymers. These insoluble strands physically contort the RBC into a sickle shape.
